statement: A 60 cm ribbon is cut into two pieces. The longer piece is 18 cm longer than the shorter piece. How long is the shorter piece?

choices.misconception: I split the ribbon in half and then took 18 cm off the 30 cm half.
I split the ribbon into two equal halves and ignored the 18 cm difference.
I found the longer piece instead of the shorter one.
I took the 18 cm away from 60 cm but forgot to share what was left between the two pieces.

hints: Draw two bars, one longer than the other by 18.
In a bar model the longer bar is a short bar plus an extra 18 cm. Remove the extra piece, and what is left is two equal short bars.
60 - 18 = 42 cm is two short pieces, so one short piece is half of 42.

solutions.reliable: Draw the short piece as a bar and the long piece as the same bar plus 18 cm. Together they make 60 cm. Take away the extra 18 cm: 60 - 18 = 42 cm is two equal short bars, so the short piece is 42 / 2 = 21 cm. Check: 21 + 39 = 60 and 39 - 21 = 18. The transferable idea: with a total and a difference, remove the difference first, then share equally.
solutions.elegant: Halfway is 30 cm, and each piece sits half the difference, 9 cm, away from halfway: the short piece is 30 - 9 = 21 cm.

whyOnTest: Sum-and-difference problems are a bar-model classic, and the trap is taking the 18 off one half.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
